correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the continuous argument in RESULT.md lines 21–63. The distributional second derivative of the mean-zero Bernoulli kernel is 1 minus the point mass, so the norm squared is the largest eigenvalue of its evaluation Gram matrix. Every two-site principal block bounds this below by 1/12 plus the largest absolute correlation. At the candidate threshold s=G(t)=−G(2t), the admissible gaps are [t,2t] and [1−2t,1−t]. Three small gaps sum to at most 6t<1, two large gaps sum to more than 1, and one large plus two small sum to at least 1 with equality only at (t,t,1−2t). Tightening the threshold eliminates this last case. Solving 5t²−3t+1/3=0 gives the stated t; the optimal Gram matrix is (1/12+s)I−s vvᵀ, v=(1,−1,1), so the upper eigenvalue is double and its eigenvectors map through the adjoint to precisely the two-dimensional norming space. Equal gaps give the asserted 1/9. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed; the result does not depend on its finite grid.

originality.rationale: There is strong statement-level coverage by the distinct indexed universal three-site circular minimax theorem. It treats the same largest-eigenvalue objective, explicitly includes mean-zero periodic H^s for s>1/2, and fixes the unique gaps by K(d)+K(2d)=0. Setting s=1 gives the record's core. The radical and eigenvalue multiplicity then follow by a quadratic and the rank-one Gram calculation, not by a separate design theorem. This is a decision about coverage, not a claim about which same-day document was first.
